```{r setup, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
suppressMessages({ library(data.table); library(ggplot2) })
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.align = "center")

PSI <- "/project/xinhe/xsun/pumseq/pumseq_processed/psi_qtl"
CG  <- file.path(PSI, "qtl_betabinomial/calibration_grid")
SEL <- file.path(PSI, "qtl_betabinomial/pc_window_selection/fold5_union_auto_noUCcalled/summary")

WINDOWS <- c(5, 20, 50); KS <- c(3, 5, 7, 10, 15)
G  <- fread(file.path(CG, "grid_calibration.tsv"))[window_kb %in% WINDOWS & npcs %in% KS]
BD <- fread(file.path(CG, "grid_by_dataset.tsv"))[window_kb %in% WINDOWS & npcs %in% KS]
QQ <- fread(file.path(CG, "grid_qq_thinned.tsv.gz"))[window_kb %in% WINDOWS & npcs %in% KS]
# every p-value, overlapping points merged at a third of a pixel (53.qq_full_page_data.R)
QA <- fread(file.path(CG, "grid_qq_allpoints_merged.tsv.gz"))[window_kb %in% WINDOWS & npcs %in% KS]
source("code/qq_full_style.R")
ST <- fread(file.path(SEL, "selection_table.tsv"))
NI <- fread(file.path(SEL, "selection_no_inheritedC.tsv"))
stopifnot(nrow(G) == 15, QQ[, uniqueN(dataset), by = .(window_kb, npcs)]$V1 == 6)

QQ[, kind := ifelse(dataset == "real", "real data", "5 permutations")]
YMAX <- max(QQ$observed); XMAX <- max(QQ$expected)
fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)

# pointwise 95% band for the order statistics of n uniform p-values, on the QQ axes
band <- function(n, expected) {
  i <- pmin(pmax(round(n * 10^(-expected) + 0.5), 1), n)
  data.table(expected = expected,
             lo = -log10(qbeta(0.975, i, n - i + 1)), hi = -log10(qbeta(0.025, i, n - i + 1)))
}

qq_plot <- function(w, k) {
  g <- G[window_kb == w & npcs == k]
  qq_panel(QA[window_kb == w & npcs == k], sprintf("+/-%d kb, k = %d PCs", w, k)) +
    labs(subtitle = sprintf("%s cis tests | permutation lambda %.3f-%.3f, real %.3f\nworst permuted -log10 p %.1f | eSites (q < 0.05): %d (%d without inherited-C sites)",
                            fmt(g$tests), g$perm_lambda_min, g$perm_lambda_max, g$real_lambda, g$worst_perm_tail,
                            ST[window_kb == w & npcs == k]$disc_q05, NI[window_kb == w & npcs == k]$eSites_clean)) +
    theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, hjust = 0.5))
}
```

# 1. What this page shows

This page checks how well the likelihood-ratio test is calibrated for each of
the 15 configurations considered for the real-data analysis: cis windows of
±5, 20 and 50 kb, and k = 3, 5, 7, 10 and 15 phenotype PCs.

**The test.** Beta-binomial LRT, with each fit started from φ = 0.01, 0.1 and
0.5 and the best kept. Covariates are the first k M-value PCs, and the
phenotype is `fold5_union_auto_noUCcalled` (10,738 sites).

**The permutations.** Each configuration was run on the real data and on 5
genome-wide permutations. A permutation shuffles each site's phenotype and PCs
together across cell lines and keeps the genotypes fixed. The same 5
permutation orders are used in every configuration. A permuted data set
contains no pU-QTL, so its p-values should follow the diagonal, and any excess
is a false positive.

**Same fits as the eSite counts.** The real-data p-values here are identical
to those of the window and PC selection scan (`47.scan_pc_window_selection.R`).
That was checked at every chr21–22 site for ±5 kb with k = 3 (466 sites) and
for ±50 kb with k = 15 (336 sites).

**What this checks, and what it does not.** These are the nominal LRT
p-values. The eSite counts in the table and plot subtitles use a different
p-value: a per-site permutation p-value under the same k. That p-value is calibrated using within-site permutations. This page checks
nominal tests; it does not establish the false discovery rate of the full
eSite selection pipeline. A null run of the full selection pipeline has not
been done.

# 2. Summary

## Discoveries across configurations

The heatmaps show **numbers of eSites**, using Storey q-values from the
100 within-site permutations. The top row includes all tested sites; the
bottom row sets aside sites flagged by untreated C reads and recalculates
q-values. This is a sensitivity analysis, not an additional fitting failure.

An **untreated-C flag** means at least one untreated cell line has >=10 reads,
>=2 C reads, and C/read fraction >=10%. These flags differ from the called
U/C sites already excluded before this scan, and do not by themselves prove
that a site is an artifact.

```{r summary, fig.width=9, fig.height=6.5}
tab <- merge(G, ST[, .(window_kb, npcs, disc_q05, disc_q10,
                       incomplete_permutations, min_valid_permutations)], by=c("window_kb","npcs"))
tab <- merge(tab, NI[, .(window_kb,npcs,eSites_clean,eSites_clean_q10)], by=c("window_kb","npcs"))
setorder(tab,window_kb,npcs)
FD <- file.path(SEL,"fit_diagnostics")
FS <- fread(file.path(FD,"real_snp_fits.tsv"))
SS <- fread(file.path(FD,"site_status.tsv"))
DD <- fread(file.path(FD,"failure_distribution.tsv"))
heat <- function(d, title, fill="Sites", columns=NULL) {
  d <- copy(d)
  d[, `:=`(pc=factor(npcs,levels=KS), window=factor(paste0("+/-",window_kb," kb"),
                levels=paste0("+/-",rev(WINDOWS)," kb")))]
  if (!"label" %in% names(d)) d[,label:=format(value,big.mark=",",trim=TRUE)]
  ggplot(d,aes(pc,window,fill=value)) + geom_tile(colour="white",linewidth=1) +
    geom_text(aes(label=label),size=4,colour="#132b43") +
    scale_fill_gradient(low="#f5f9fc",high="#80bedb",name=fill) +
    labs(x="Number of phenotype PCs",y="Cis window",title=title) +
    theme_minimal(base_size=12) + theme(panel.grid=element_blank(),
      strip.text=element_text(face="bold"),plot.title=element_text(face="bold"))
}
E <- rbindlist(list(
 tab[,.(window_kb,npcs,value=disc_q05,cutoff="q < 0.05",set="All tested sites")],
 tab[,.(window_kb,npcs,value=disc_q10,cutoff="q < 0.10",set="All tested sites")],
 tab[,.(window_kb,npcs,value=eSites_clean,cutoff="q < 0.05",set="Untreated-C flags set aside")],
 tab[,.(window_kb,npcs,value=eSites_clean_q10,cutoff="q < 0.10",set="Untreated-C flags set aside")]))
E[,set:=factor(set,levels=c("All tested sites","Untreated-C flags set aside"))]
heat(E,"eSites by window, PC count and q-value cutoff","eSites") + facet_grid(set~cutoff)
```

## Sites extreme in both real and permuted data

An **extreme site** has a minimum nominal p-value <1e-10 in the real data
and in at least one of the five genome-wide permutations. This flags an
extreme tail in the calibration check; it is distinct from a failed fit and
from an eSite passing a q-value cutoff.

```{r extreme-heatmap, fig.width=8, fig.height=3.2}
heat(tab[,.(window_kb,npcs,value=problematic)],
     "Sites extreme in both real and permuted data")
```

## Fitting failures

Fits use three starting values and maximum likelihood throughout. A failed
fit is one rejected by the production fitter, not a small or near-zero phi
estimate. A near-zero phi can be a valid fitted result.

- **Null fit failed:** the model without genotype was rejected. The site
  cannot be tested. This fit is shared across windows, so its count is
  shown once per PC setting.
- **All SNP fits failed:** the null fit succeeded but no SNP in the indicated
  window produced a finite nominal p-value. The site has no result in that window.
- **Any SNP fit failed:** at least one genotype-model fit failed. This includes
  the all-failed sites; other affected sites can still have a valid result.
- **Incomplete permutations:** a tested site had fewer than 100 finite
  within-site permutation minima. This is a separate diagnostic, not a count
  of failed individual permutation-SNP fits.

SNP-fit counts are conditional on the null fit succeeding. Fewer failed SNP
fits at higher PC counts therefore do not mean fitting improved: more sites
have already been lost at the null-fit stage.

Sites skipped because no suitable cis SNP exists are not fitting failures.
These diagnostics describe the selection scan, rather than the separate
five genome-wide calibration runs.

```{r null-fit-failures, fig.width=8, fig.height=3.5}
NS <- SS[,.(total=sum(N),null_failed=sum(N[status=="null_fit_failed"]),
            skipped=sum(N[status %in% c("no_cis_snp","no_common_cis_snp","too_few_cell_lines")])),by=npcs]
NS[,eligible:=total-skipped]
NS[,label:=sprintf("%s / %s\n(%.1f%%)",fmt(null_failed),fmt(eligible),100*null_failed/eligible)]
ggplot(NS,aes(factor(npcs,levels=KS),100*null_failed/eligible)) +
 geom_col(fill="#4288ab",width=.65) + geom_text(aes(label=label),vjust=-.25,size=3.6) +
 scale_y_continuous(expand=expansion(mult=c(0,.22))) +
 labs(x="Number of phenotype PCs",y="Null fits rejected (%)",
      title="Null-fit failures increase with PC count",
      subtitle="Labels: rejected / sites with suitable cis SNPs within 50 kb") +
 theme_minimal(base_size=12)
```

```{r failure-heatmaps, fig.width=8, fig.height=3.2}
F <- rbindlist(list(
 FS[,.(window_kb,npcs,value=sites_all_failed,metric="Sites: all SNP fits failed")],
 FS[,.(window_kb,npcs,value=sites_any_failed,metric="Sites: any SNP fit failed")],
 FS[,.(window_kb,npcs,value=failed,metric="Failed SNP fits")],
 tab[,.(window_kb,npcs,value=incomplete_permutations,metric="Sites: incomplete permutations")]))
F[,metric:=factor(metric,levels=unique(metric))]
# Each panel gets a separate colour scale because counts have different units.
for (m in levels(F$metric)) print(heat(F[metric==m],m) +
  theme(plot.title=element_text(size=12)))
```

### How failures are distributed {.tabset}

The left panel shows **all eligible sites**; the right panel shows **failed
sites at each PC setting**. A failed site has a rejected null fit or no
successful SNP fit within 50 kb. Sites skipped because no suitable cis SNP
exists are excluded from both groups.

Each cell shows the number of sites and their percentage within that column.
Every column sums to 100% before rounding. The eligible-site distribution is
the same for all PC settings and is shown once. A bin is overrepresented among
failures when its percentage in a failed-site column exceeds the percentage
in the eligible-site column. This compares distributions, rather than the
probability that a site in that bin fails.

For example, sites with 40-49 covered cell lines account for **46.9% of all
eligible sites**, but **65.9% of failures at 15 PCs** (1.41 times their baseline
share). Sites covered in all 50 cell lines account for 43.6% of eligible sites
and 11.3% of failures at 15 PCs. Thus, the large failure count in the 40-49 bin
reflects both its size and its overrepresentation among failures. These
comparisons do not separate sample coverage from read depth or other site
characteristics.

Read depth is total reads divided by the number of covered cell lines.
The failure set is determined separately for each PC setting.

```{r distribution-helper, include=FALSE}
distribution_plot <- function(v, bins, title, ylab) {
 d <- copy(DD[variable==v])
 # The same eligible sites were considered under each PC configuration.
 stopifnot(all(d[,uniqueN(sites),by=bin]$V1==1L))
 d[,total_failed:=sum(failed),by=npcs]
 stopifnot(all(d$total_failed>0), !anyNA(d$bin))
 failures <- d[,.(bin,column=as.character(npcs),count=failed,
                 share=100*failed/total_failed,group="Failed sites")]
 baseline <- d[npcs==KS[1],.(bin,column="All",count=sites,
                            share=100*sites/sum(sites),group="All eligible sites")]
 plot_data <- rbindlist(list(baseline,failures))
 stopifnot(all(abs(plot_data[,sum(share),by=.(group,column)]$V1-100)<1e-8))
 plot_data[,`:=`(column=factor(column,levels=c("All",as.character(KS))),
                 bin=factor(bin,levels=rev(bins)),
                 group=factor(group,levels=c("All eligible sites","Failed sites")))]
 stopifnot(!anyNA(plot_data$bin))
 plot_data[,label:=sprintf("%d sites\n%.1f%%",count,share)]
 ggplot(plot_data,aes(column,bin,fill=share)) + geom_tile(colour="white",linewidth=.8) +
 geom_text(aes(label=label),size=3.1) +
 facet_grid(~group,scales="free_x",space="free_x") +
 scale_fill_gradient(low="#fff7ec",high="#d66a36",limits=c(0,100),name="Share of sites (%)") +
 labs(x="All eligible sites / failed sites by number of phenotype PCs",y=ylab,title=title,
      subtitle="Each column sums to 100%; compare failed-site shares with the eligible-site baseline") +
 theme_minimal(base_size=11) + theme(panel.grid=element_blank(),
      strip.text=element_text(face="bold"),panel.spacing.x=grid::unit(.6,"lines"))
}
```

### Rejection reasons

These are diagnostic rejection reasons, not a proof of a single underlying
biological cause. The SNP-fit counts count model fits; the null-fit counts
count sites. Incomplete permutations are not included here.

```{r failure-reasons}
NR <- fread(file.path(FD,"null_failure_reasons.tsv"))
SR <- fread(file.path(FD,"real_snp_failure_reasons.tsv"))[window_kb==50]
setnames(NR,c("null_fail_code","N"),c("fail_code","n"))
R <- rbindlist(list(NR[,.(npcs,fail_code,n,type="Null fits (sites)")],
                   SR[,.(npcs,fail_code,n,type="SNP fits (50 kb)")]))
reason_labels <- c(`1`="Starting binomial GLM rejected",`2`="All optimizer starts discarded",
 `3`="Degenerate optimum",`4`="Coefficient exceeded limit",
 `5`="Iteration limit near phi=0 (binomial boundary diagnostic)",
 `8`="Diagnostic rerun succeeded",`9`="Diagnostic rerun errored")
R[,reason:=unname(reason_labels[as.character(fail_code)])]
stopifnot(!anyNA(R$reason))
knitr::kable(dcast(R,type+reason~npcs,value.var="n",fill=0),
 caption="Rejected fits by reason and number of PCs. SNP models use the widest window.")
```

### Calibration across configurations

```{r lambdaplot, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.2}
L <- BD[dataset != "real", .(lo = min(lambda), hi = max(lambda), mid = median(lambda)), by = .(window_kb, npcs)]
L[, window := factor(sprintf("%d kb", window_kb), levels = sprintf("%d kb", WINDOWS))]
ggplot(L, aes(npcs, mid, colour = window)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, colour = "grey55", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), width = 0.35, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("5 kb" = "#1f4e9c", "20 kb" = "#2c8a4a", "50 kb" = "#d98c00"), name = "cis window") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = KS) +
  labs(x = "phenotype PCs (k)", y = "genomic-control lambda",
       title = "Calibration under permutation",
       subtitle = "Point = median over the 5 permutations, bar = range. Dashed line = 1 (perfect calibration).") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

# 3. QQ plots, one per configuration {.tabset}

Each panel shows every cis test on the real data (teal) and on the 5
permutations (light blue), and has its own y-axis. Every p-value is included.
There are 1.75 to 17.6 million per configuration, so points that would land on
the same spot of the figure (within a third of a pixel) are drawn once; the
picture is the same as plotting each one.

## ±5 kb

```{r qq5, results="asis", fig.width=7, fig.height=5.6}
for (k in KS) { cat(sprintf("\n\n### k = %d\n\n", k)); print(qq_plot(5, k)); cat("\n\n") }
```

## ±20 kb

```{r qq20, results="asis", fig.width=7, fig.height=5.6}
for (k in KS) { cat(sprintf("\n\n### k = %d\n\n", k)); print(qq_plot(20, k)); cat("\n\n") }
```

## ±50 kb

```{r qq50, results="asis", fig.width=7, fig.height=5.6}
for (k in KS) { cat(sprintf("\n\n### k = %d\n\n", k)); print(qq_plot(50, k)); cat("\n\n") }
```

# 4. Reading the plots

```{r reading}
r <- G[, .(lam = sprintf("%.2f-%.2f", min(perm_lambda_min), max(perm_lambda_max))), by = npcs][order(npcs)]
```

- **The bulk of the test is inflated as k grows, in every window.** Permutation
  lambda is `r r[npcs == 3]$lam` at k = 3, `r r[npcs == 5]$lam` at k = 5,
  `r r[npcs == 7]$lam` at k = 7, `r r[npcs == 10]$lam` at k = 10 and
  `r r[npcs == 15]$lam` at k = 15. The window changes it very little.
- **Every configuration has a permuted tail beyond chance.** The worst
  permuted −log10 p is 11.3–25.9, against an expected maximum of about 6–7. At
  ±5 kb with k = 3, those permuted outliers are sites where one cell line
  supplies most of the converted reads; many are in the immunoglobulin and MHC
  regions. The tail is lowest at k = 3, at 11.3 in all three windows. At k = 10
  and 15 it grows with the window, as do the sites extreme in both real and
  permuted data (`r tab[npcs == 15 & window_kb == 50]$problematic` at ±50 kb,
  k = 15).
- **The real data separate clearly from the permutations** in every
  configuration, with real −log10 p up to `r sprintf("%.0f", max(G$real_tail))`.
  But about 60% of the eSites have untreated-C flags. These may include
  genotype-associated background conversion, so the real-data tail should
  not automatically be interpreted as pU-QTL signal.

Data: `calibration_grid/grid_calibration.tsv`, `grid_by_dataset.tsv` and
`grid_qq_thinned.tsv.gz` (built by `27.calibration_grid_summary.R` from
`8.calibration_site_resolved.R` runs). eSites come from
`pc_window_selection/fold5_union_auto_noUCcalled/summary/` (`48.pc_window_selection_summary.R`
and `50.selection_inheritedC_setaside.R`).

Fit diagnostics are reconstructed by `55.pc_window_failure_summary.R` from
the saved real-data `_sites` and `_snps` logs. Aggregated tables and per-site
diagnostics are in `summary/fit_diagnostics/`. The 15 tested-site counts
were checked against `selection_table.tsv`.
